samples.summary: Self-removal action is presented with the owner-facing label "Remove member". For a non-owner the only button shown is the one that removes themselves, which semantically is "Leave workspace". Reusing the moderation label (and its aria-label) for a self-leave action is a UI/semantic fit mismatch, and the new test bakes that label into an assertion, making it harder to correct later.

Capability is re-derived on the client from the members list rather than coming from the server, unlike the established pattern elsewhere in this frontend where the backend ships an explicit capability flag (documents carry `canManage`, see packages/frontend/src/types/documents.ts:54 and document-list.tsx:956). The gating added here is correct as UI affordance only (backend `assertOwner` still enforces), but it diverges from the repo's server-driven-capability approach and duplicates ownership logic in the client.
samples.evidence: const isOwner = me && workspace?.members.some((m) => m.user.id === me.id && m.role === "owner");

samples.summary: `isOwner` is falsy while the `me` and `workspace` queries are still resolving, so for an actual owner the Invites section (and its query) is initially not rendered/enabled and then pops in once both queries settle. This is a layout-flicker consequence of gating render on derived, async-dependent state; the pre-existing API Keys section has the same shape, so the change extends rather than introduces the pattern, but a single `isOwner === undefined` loading branch would fit better.

Non-owners now see no Invites section at all and no explanation; combined with the members table showing only their own trash icon, the settings page silently differs by role. No design doc records the intended per-role settings surface (docs/design/sharing.md documents a role/permission matrix for sharing but not workspace-settings visibility), so there is nothing to check this UI against. Likely fine as a bugfix, but worth a line in the canonical doc if role-gated settings UI is meant to be a rule.
